final_synthesis: Healthy adults taking vitamin D supplements for disease prevention may not see the benefits they expect. A randomised trial involving 25,871 participants found that daily supplementation with 2,000 IU of vitamin D3 did not lower the incidence of invasive cancer or major cardiovascular events compared to placebo [S1]. Observational studies have linked low vitamin D levels to various diseases, but these findings do not necessarily imply causation; randomised trials have largely failed to confirm benefits in healthy individuals who are already sufficient in vitamin D [S5][S4]. While vitamin D supplementation clearly benefits those deficient, preventing conditions like rickets and osteomalacia, the evidence for additional health benefits in non-deficient adults is unproven [S3][S4].
